Build prompt

Rebuild this interaction 1:1: Honk's emoji battle rage tap - rapid tapping on the emoji keyboard unleashes an emoji storm that floods the entire screen with flying emojis until it fully covers the chat, then drains away.

## Integration
Integration: stack-agnostic spec - springs given as stiffness/damping, timed motions as duration + curve; map every value to your framework and animation library of choice.

## Scene
Honk chat with Alex: blue "battle?" bubble, the emoji keyboard grid open at the bottom. During the storm, hundreds of emojis (smileys, flames, kisses, 100s, hands) fly across the whole screen, stacking into a dense layer that completely covers the chat - the bubble barely peeks through - before they clear.

## Motion spec
Pattern: tap-driven emoji flood with saturation and drain.
- Each rapid tap on an emoji key launches 3-5 of that emoji from the keyboard area upward with random velocity (angle 60-120deg, speed 400-700pt/s), random scale (0.6-1.4) and spin (+-180deg/s).
- Emojis arc with light gravity, bounce softly off screen edges (damping 0.6), and linger, drifting; sustained rage-tapping accumulates them faster than they fade until the screen is a solid emoji layer (~200+ live sprites).
- Each emoji pulses on spawn (scale 0 -> 1.2 -> 1, 150ms).
- Storm end (tapping stops ~1s): all emojis simultaneously get gravity again and rain down off the bottom of the screen over ~800ms, fading in the last 300ms; the chat emerges clean underneath.

## Calibration
- Density is the joke - the storm must actually reach near-total coverage before draining.
- The tapped emoji dominates the mix (about 70% tapped glyph, 30% random others).

## Reduced motion
A capped burst of 20 emojis that fade in place (600ms); no accumulation.

## Don't miss
- The emoji keyboard stays open and tappable through the whole storm.
- The drain is a clean sweep - nothing is left on screen after it.
